facts.resource_count_limit: Exact source-listed labels, deduplicated within each match. They include uncertain or offensive entries and are not verified forced-resource frequencies.
facts.cc_count_limit: Literal mentions in observed notes, including negated/uncertain/post-death mentions. These are search aids, not counts of landed CC.

hypotheses.statement: One opening target also explains every reported enemy kill in wins.
hypotheses.limitation: Descriptive endpoint comparison. Does not establish intended kill target, causes, or conditional win probability.

hypotheses.statement: Low enemy health and usable friendly damage overlap with enough partner disruption to prevent recovery. Neither a fixed kill target nor an empty pair of Trinkets is established as necessary.
hypotheses.limitation: The nearly balanced enemy-kill split rejects a single compulsory kill target. Ready Trinkets, active healing and short control gaps occur in wins. Counter-kills after a friendly death must be separated from intact-team conversions.

hypotheses.statement: A stronger fixed resource/target/control prerequisite is necessary.
hypotheses.limitation: The nearly balanced enemy-kill split rejects a single compulsory kill target. Ready Trinkets, active healing and short control gaps occur in wins. Counter-kills after a friendly death must be separated from intact-team conversions.

opening_target.text: Subtlety Rogue; recorded in 76/104 games. This is the labeled opening target, not necessarily the first sustained coordinated damage.

initial_objective.text: Create effective damage before countercontrol costs a teammate; use pressure on the exposed Rogue to find either a Rogue finish or a Priest conversion.

win_condition.text: Low enemy health and usable friendly damage overlap with enough partner disruption to prevent recovery. Neither a fixed kill target nor an empty pair of Trinkets is established as necessary.

manufacture.text: Rogue is the most frequent opener. Pressure with Priest disruption, then retain Rogue or transfer to Priest when Rogue control supports a real damage window.

conversion.text: Finish the opponent whose health pressure can be sustained; repeated Rogue-control/Priest-swap and Priest-control/Rogue-finish sequences both occur.

reset.text: Healing often restores the first window. Stabilise and renew a same-target attempt or a supported switch; a full stealth reset is not established as the universal recovery pattern.

assessment.text: A conditional escape resource; late or unused escapes do not define whether the target can die.

failure_modes.text: Control or escape extraction occurs too late, or produces little damage before friendly Priest death.
The target survives at very low health as partner control expires; a friendly dies before the finish.

automatic_candidates.signal: Verified cast/aura, present health, or an observed control start/end
automatic_candidates.scope: Raw events only; not strategic intent or reliable absence of an enemy cooldown.
automatic_candidates.limitation: No addon implementation or API testing was performed; no automatic transition is certified.

manual_possible.confirmation: A meaningful enemy health window, current partner control and friendly readiness overlap.
Target recovered or became protected; team needs a new usable attempt.

web_only: Full comparison with losses and unresolved evidence

uncertainties: The nearly balanced enemy-kill split rejects a single compulsory kill target. Ready Trinkets, active healing and short control gaps occur in wins. Counter-kills after a friendly death must be separated from intact-team conversions.
Precise Priest/Rogue division of labour by phase is mostly unknown.
Exact runtime detection reliability on Warmane 3.3.5 is untested.
